name: glb-update-original
description: GE4 real-env verification of the GLB designer's 'Update original' round-trip (`ui/glbEditor/GlbDesignerDialog.tsx` -> `furniture/glbEdit/saveAsset.ts:exportAndSaveAsset(overwriteId)` -> `state/slices/userAssetsSlice.ts:replaceUserFurniture`). Pro mode. Creates a real user asset (a 0.8 m box) via the designer save path, places an instance of it in the Living/Dining room editor, then re-opens the designer, picks that asset as the 'Start from' source, scales it 2x, toggles the 'Update original' switch, and clicks 'Update original'. Asserts the REAL round-trip against the live Zustand store, NOT toast text: (1) the def count did NOT grow (no duplicate catalog entry) — `userFurniture.length` stays at the post-create baseline; (2) the SAME def id now carries the new geometry — its `defaultFootprint.w` ~doubled AND its `assetId` changed (a fresh GLB blob was written under the same id); (3) the previously placed instance still resolves — `items` still holds an item whose `defId` is that same def id. Screenshots the placed instance in the room BEFORE and AFTER the update so the size change is visible in the 3D scene. NOTE: both the initial 'Save asset' and the 'Update original' saves are triggered via DOM `.click()` evals because those buttons live at the bottom of the scrolling right panel (below the fold) — the coordinate text-click would miss them (see glb-designer-simple.json's click-save comment + the playbook gotcha). The source-model picker is the custom `ui/controls/Select` (not a native <select>): driven by clicking its `button[aria-label='Source model']` trigger then the `[role='option']` whose label matches. The 'Recolour parts' section only renders once the source GLB has loaded into the preview (its named meshes populate `meshNames`), so the scenario waits on that text as the load gate before scaling + saving — this guarantees the re-exported GLB actually contains the original geometry (not an empty object) so placed instances can't silently lose their mesh.

steps.name: capture-def
steps.comment: Capture the created def's id, original footprint width, original assetId, and the post-create catalog length — the baselines the update assertions compare against.
steps.eval: (function(){ const s = window.__store.getState(); const def = s.userFurniture.find(d => d.name === 'IXT Update RT' && d.source === 'user'); if (!def) throw new Error('created def missing'); window.__updDefId = def.id; window.__origFpW = def.defaultFootprint.w; window.__origAssetId = def.assetId; window.__afterCreateLen = s.userFurniture.length; if (!(window.__origFpW > 0)) throw new Error('bad original footprint ' + window.__origFpW); })()

steps.name: assert-roundtrip
steps.comment: The REAL round-trip proof: (1) no duplicate — length stays at the post-create baseline; (2) same def id carries new geometry — footprint scaled by ~2x EXACTLY (a guard against the fixed scale-double-application bug that produced 4x/8x), a fresh assetId, AND the name preserved (guard against the fixed name-clobber-to-'Custom asset' bug); (3) placed instance still resolves to the same def id.

waitFor.store: state.userFurniture.length === window.__afterCreateLen && (state.userFurniture.find(d => d.id === window.__updDefId)?.defaultFootprint.w ?? 0) > window.__origFpW * 1.7 && (state.userFurniture.find(d => d.id === window.__updDefId)?.defaultFootprint.w ?? 0) < window.__origFpW * 2.4 && state.userFurniture.find(d => d.id === window.__updDefId)?.assetId !== window.__origAssetId && state.userFurniture.find(d => d.id === window.__updDefId)?.name === 'IXT Update RT' && state.items.some(it => it.defId === window.__updDefId)

steps.failMessage: Update original should replace the def in place (same id, ~2x footprint EXACTLY, fresh assetId, name preserved) WITHOUT growing the catalog, and the placed instance must still reference it
